chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, both together, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Ya'qub al-Ahmar who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'May I be your ransom! Worries and other matters have afflicted me, until nothing of goodness remains without a portion of it having slipped away from me — even the Quran, a portion of it has slipped away from me.'

He (the narrator) said: And he (the Imam) was alarmed when I mentioned the Quran. Then he said: 'Indeed a man forgets a chapter from the Quran, and it will come to him on the Day of Resurrection until it appears before him from a level among some of the levels, and says: Peace be upon you. He will say: And upon you peace — who are you? It will say: I am Chapter such-and-such. You wasted me and abandoned me. Had you but held fast to me, I would have brought you to this level.' Then he gestured with his finger.

Then he said: 'You must adhere to the Quran — learn it! For among the people is one who learns the Quran so that it may be said, 'So-and-so is a reciter'; and among them is one who learns it seeking praise for his voice, so it is said 'So-and-so has a beautiful voice' — and there is no good in that. And among them is one who learns it and stands by it during his night and his day, not caring who knows of that and who does not.'

key_terms.تَفَلَّتَ: Slipped away/escaped — refers to Quran verses or good deeds escaping one's grasp due to neglect
key_terms.تَمَسَّكَ: To hold fast/adhere — important Quranic concept of clinging to the divine word
key_terms.دَرَجَة: Level/rank in Paradise — spiritual stations earned by deeds
key_terms.قَارِئ: Reciter/reader of Quran — one who has memorized or regularly recites it
key_terms.يُبَالِي: To care/concern oneself with — the sincere learner is indifferent to the opinions of others

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about forgetting the Quran and the consequences on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Ya'qub al-Ahmar reports to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) that worldly worries have caused him to forget portions of the Quran. The Imam is visibly alarmed at the mention of forgetting the Quran and responds with a vivid eschatological narrative: on the Day of Resurrection, the very chapters of the Quran that a person forgot will appear and greet them, lamenting that had the person adhered to them, they would have elevated him to a high rank. The Imam then exhorts the companions to learn the Quran sincerely — not for reputation or to be praised for a beautiful recitation voice, but to practice it during the night and day without concern for what others think. This reflects the broader Shia emphasis on sincere, lived engagement with the Quran as distinct from performative piety.
word_analysis: a beautiful voice/praise for his voice

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Khalid and Al Husayn Bin Saeed, altogether from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Yahya Al Halby, from Abdullah Bin Muskan, from Yaqoub Al Ahmar who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! Worries and other things hit me, and there does not remain anything from the goodness except a section from it has escaped from me, even the Quran, a section from it has escaped from me (as well)’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So he<sup>asws</sup> was shocked at that when I mentioned the Quran. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The man forgets the Chapter from the Quran, so it would come to him on the Day of Judgment until it displays itself upon him from a Level from some of the Levels, and it would be saying: ‘The greetings be upon you’. So he would be saying, ‘And upon you be the greetings. Who are you?’ So it would be saying: ‘I am Chapter such and such. You wasted me and neglected me. But, had you attached yourself with me, I would have caused you to reach to this Level’. Then it would gesture by its fingers.

Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘(It is) upon you with the Quran. From the people is one who learns the Quran in order for it to be said, ‘So and so is a reciter’; and from them is the one who learns it, and he seeks the voice by it, so it is said to him, ‘So and so and an excellent voice’, and there is no goodness in that; and from them is the one who learns it, so he stands by it during his night and his day, not caring who knows of that and who does not know of that’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Khalid and al-Husayn ibn Sa’id all from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Yahya al-Halabi from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muskan from Ya’qub al-Ahmar who has said the following:
“Once I said to abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) ‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, I am facing such problems and difficulties that I forget so many good things even some of the Holy Quran.’

The Imam was shocked upon my mentioning the Holy Quran and said, ‘If a man forgets a chapter of the Holy Quran, on the Day of Judgment that chapter will appear to him with a certain rank and offers him the greeting of peace. The man will ask, ‘Who are you?’ The chapter of the Holy Quran will say, ‘I am chapter so and so of the Holy Quran which you forgot, and I wish you had not forgotten me; today I could have taken you to such and such high ranks. He will point to a certain rank.’

The Imam then said, ‘You must hold fast to the Holy Quran and learn it. Certain people learn the Holy Quran so that others call him a very good reader of the Holy Quran. Others learn the Holy Quran so that people praise him for his vocal attractiveness in reciting the Holy Quran. There is nothing good in all of this. Certain people learn the Holy Quran and at night they stand upon their feet with the Holy Quran as well as during the day and they are not concerned whether others know this about them or not.’”
